input.summary: Source-fidelity preflight v10 (functional-surface-geometry) completed over the full record: input/brief.md, input/conversation.md (which ends mid-sentence at "The difference between", the complete sentence being present in disclosure.md), input/disclosure.md, input/request.md, all ten draft sections (title, cross-reference, government support, field, background, summary, drawings, detailed description, 22 claims, abstract), draft/numerals.md, and figure briefs FIG-1 through FIG-7. Every limitation of independent claims 1, 13, and 18 and of dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, and 19-22 was traced to an exact affirmative USER passage in the disclosure: rail with flat lower face/upper face/first and second ends/longitudinal slot through the rail; printed distance marks beside the slot; fence at the first end, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the edge; two-screw releasable mounting in two corresponding holes and the invert-and-reinstall reversal moving the projecting portion between longitudinal sides while the marked face stays up; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback of every guided hole by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages with lower keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical drill bushing per carriage with a bore through the carriage registering with the slot; the two bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail with a shank through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping the rail between carriage and shoe and releasing on loosening; a pointer per carriage aligned with its bore axis and read against the same marks, the reading difference being center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the full use sequence; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list plus hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no motor/battery/sensor/network limitation. All 27 numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) carry one meaning each, every one appears in at least one figure brief and in the description, and every parenthetical figure call-out in the detailed description (14 in FIG. 4; 12, 72, 74, 78, 80 in FIG. 3; 52, 54, 58, 60 in FIG. 5; 18, 62, 82 in FIG. 2; 34, 36 in FIG. 6; 24, 26, 94 in FIG. 7; 32, 58, 92 in FIG. 1) matches that brief's numeral list. Section lines were checked end to end: FIG-2 places designation 3 at both endpoints of the line crossing carriage 70 and designation 5 at both endpoints of the line crossing carriage 50, and "line 3-3"/"line 5-5" are used identically in draft/07-drawings.md, the detailed description, and the FIG-3 and FIG-5 briefs, with the sectioned carriage matching in each. Schematic-outline choices (plain round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence and carriage bodies, elongated slot opening, ragged break line, V-notch) were tested against the depiction-convention rule: each is labeled "shown schematically" in the brief, the claims and description remain shape-neutral, no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, or contact topology is verbalized, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language was imported into the application text. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain; the abstract is 149 words; brief-mandated terminology (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch) is preserved; and the "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support sections match the filing brief. Three defects are reported: one critical untraced result assertion that the three jig settings are mutually non-interfering (the source assigns two of the three parameters to the single pointer-reading feature and never states independence), one minor untraced fastening topology in the FIG-6 brief (screws passing through the fence to engage rail-carried holes), and one minor internal ordering contradiction between the Summary's "before both clamp knobs are tightened" and the tighten-then-place-then-align sequence used in the Summary's own final paragraph, the detailed description, and method claim 18. Everything else in the ledger traced cleanly.

findings.title: Untraced assertion that the three jig settings are mutually independent and do not disturb one another
findings.where: draft/06-summary.md, final sentence of the paragraph beginning "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint"; draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "The three settings that the jig makes are separate from one another" (final sentence)
findings.detail: The candidate asserts, as a property of the invention, that the setback setting, the spacing/position setting, and the centerline setting are made against three separate features and are mutually non-interfering. No affirmative USER passage states this. The disclosure states only which feature controls which parameter, and states one specific independence (the spacer plate does not change hole separation). The disclosure in fact assigns two of the three parameters to a single feature - the pointer readings control both hole separation and the position of the pair - so the categorical non-interference statement is not merely untraced but is in tension with the source allocation and with the candidate's own procedure, in which changing the spacing requires re-centering the readings about the transverse center index.
findings.evidence: Candidate (Summary): "These three settings are made against three separate features of the jig and do not interfere with one another." Candidate (Detailed Description): "Changing one of the three settings does not disturb the other two." Nearest source passages, which do not support the assertion: "The fence controls setback from the workpiece edge, while the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." and "The spacer plate has parallel opposite faces and changes the setback of every guided hole by its thickness without changing the separation between the holes." No source passage states that the three settings are independent of one another.
findings.fix: Delete both sentences. In draft/06-summary.md end that paragraph after "...while the two pointer readings control the hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." In draft/08-detailed-description.md end that paragraph after "...set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." No replacement text is needed; the retained sentences already state the per-feature control that the source discloses.

findings.title: FIG-6 brief verbalizes an undisclosed screw-and-hole fastening topology
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, final sentence of the body text
findings.detail: The figure brief states the direction of screw passage and the member that receives the threads: the screws pass through the fence and engage holes carried by the rail. The disclosure discloses only that two screws are received in two corresponding holes and does not say which member carries the holes or which member the screws pass through. The description and claims are correspondingly silent, so the brief is the only place this connection is asserted. Screw-passage direction and thread engagement are a connection conveying technical substance and must be traced. Placing the two mounting holes 36 at the rail's first end is retained as the natural reading of the source sentence ("secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes") and because an exploded view must show the disclosed holes somewhere.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-6 brief): "Two screws 34 are shown, which pass through the fence 30 to engage the mounting holes 36." Nearest source passage: "It is secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes." The source does not state that the screws pass through the fence, nor that the fence lacks the holes. Candidate description is neutral and remains so: "the fence 30 is releasably secured to the first end of the rail 10 by two screws 34 received in two corresponding mounting holes 36."
findings.fix: Replace the final sentence of figures/FIG-6.md with: "Two screws 34 are shown aligned with the two mounting holes 36 by which the fence 30 is secured to the first end of the rail 10." Leave the preceding sentence ("The end of the rail 10 has two mounting holes 36.") unchanged and make no change to the description or claims.

findings.title: Summary contradicts its own use sequence, the detailed description, and method claim 18 on when the centerline alignment occurs
findings.where: draft/06-summary.md, paragraph beginning "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint" versus the final "In use" paragraph of the same section; draft/08-detailed-description.md use paragraphs; draft/09-claims.md claim 18
findings.detail: One Summary paragraph states that the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the workpiece centerline before both clamp knobs are tightened. Two paragraphs later the same section recites the opposite order - tighten both knobs, then place the jig, then align with the centerline - and the detailed description and method claim 18 both recite that same tighten-then-place-then-align order. The document therefore states two mutually exclusive sequences for the same operation, and the Summary's version is inconsistent with the sequence recited in the only independent method claim.
findings.evidence: Candidate (Summary): "The transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with a centerline marked on the workpiece before both clamp knobs are tightened, so that the guided holes, whose pointer readings lie at equal distances on opposite sides of the transverse center index, are centered about the transverse center index." Candidate (Summary, final paragraph): "...tightens both clamp knobs, places the flat lower face on the workpiece with the fence or the installed spacer plate pressed against the selected edge, aligns the sight notch and the transverse center index with the centerline, and drills through both drill bushings." Candidate (claim 18): "tightening the clamp knob of each of the first guide carriage and the second guide carriage...; placing the flat lower face on the front face...; moving the drilling jig along the straight edge until the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the centerline".
findings.fix: In draft/06-summary.md, delete the ordering clause so the sentence reads: "The transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with a centerline marked on the workpiece, so that the guided holes, whose pointer readings lie at equal distances on opposite sides of the transverse center index, are centered about the transverse center index." Leave the final "In use" paragraph, the detailed description, and claim 18 unchanged.
